what_it_does: Local-GS accelerates training of 3D Gaussian Splatting on edge devices (phones, drones) where memory is severely limited. Traditional training requires processing Gaussians in depth order (far to near) because overlapping Gaussians affect each other's gradients, enforcing sequential processing and preventing parallelism. Local-GS breaks this dependency by introducing order-independent rendering: instead of globally sorting by depth, it groups Gaussians by locality (nearby positions) and processes each group independently in parallel, since Gaussians far apart don't interfere. It also adds unified training-rendering cores that perform gradient computation and pixel updates simultaneously without storing large intermediate buffers, dramatically reducing memory and enabling efficient parallel hardware execution.
